question: When a patient on leprosy MDT develops a Type 1 (reversal) lepra reaction, the correct management is to continue MDT unchanged while adding prednisolone for reaction control.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Reconsider. Stopping MDT for a lepra reaction is a dangerous error. The reaction is an immune-mediated event, not drug toxicity — MDT continues unchanged while corticosteroids manage the inflammation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. MDT must NOT be stopped during lepra reactions — stopping increases the risk of relapse and resistance. Prednisolone (40–60mg/day tapered over months) is added to control the immune-mediated inflammation.
